Colour Palettes and Finishes to Elevate Office Spaces

Once you've chosen the style of wall art, colour choice and finishes become essential to achieve a considered look. Trending office wall decor ideas lean towards soothing colour palettes that support concentration whilst still providing visual interest. The relationship between colour and productivity is well documented — cool tones reduce cortisol levels, whilst warm neutrals create a sense of psychological safety that helps people settle into focused work more quickly.

Calming Colour Palettes

Calming tones help reduce stress and increase focus. Soft blues are familiar and trustworthy, making them perfect for professional settings. Earthy greens bring the outdoors inside, creating a balanced atmosphere that many people find restorative during long working hours. Warm greys and beige are neutral yet comforting, offering a solid backdrop that allows the art itself to take centre stage without competing with the walls.

Popular Finishes in Wall Art

The finish of your wall decor can alter the feel of a room dramatically. Matte finishes soften glare and are ideal for bright or sunlit rooms. Satin or semi-gloss adds a subtle sheen and depth that works well in spaces with controlled lighting. Metallic frames or accents bring a modern, sophisticated edge that suits contemporary and industrial-style offices particularly well. For those who love texture, wall panels with natural finishes offer an on-trend choice that adds dimension and beautifully complements framed wall art.

How to Decorate Office Walls on a Budget

Not everyone has a huge budget to refresh their office walls, but that doesn't mean you need to compromise style or professionalism. The most cost-effective approach is to invest in one or two genuinely good pieces rather than filling the space with cheaper items that date quickly. Here are some practical office wall decor ideas that won't break the bank.

Printable Art and DIY Projects

Download high-quality printables from reputable sources for as little as a few pounds, then invest in good-quality frames separately to add polish. Use washi tape or simple shelving to create custom displays that feel intentional rather than improvised. The key is consistency — choosing printables within the same colour family or visual style makes even a low-budget arrangement look curated and deliberate.

Thrift and Upcycle

Second-hand stores often have unique art pieces and vintage frames that simply need a fresh coat of paint or a new mount to look current. Reframing older artworks in a consistent frame style — all black, all natural wood, or all white — instantly unifies a mixed collection and gives it a gallery-like quality. This approach is also more sustainable, which aligns well with the values of many modern workplaces.

Focus on One Statement Piece

Instead of multiple items, invest in one larger piece that defines your space. This approach focuses spending where it counts and has a big visual impact without requiring careful arrangement of multiple frames. A single well-chosen piece also ages better than trend-led collections, making it a smarter long-term investment for any office. For affordable options in office wall art, browse our office decor gallery where you can find a wide price range.


SHOP HERE

How Do I Choose Office Wall Decor Ideas That Match My Brand?

When your workspace is a reflection of your business, choosing office wall decor ideas means aligning the art to your brand identity. This leaves a strong impression on clients and employees alike. The most effective brand-aligned offices don't feel like showrooms — they feel like spaces where the values of the business are quietly present in every detail, including what hangs on the walls.

Use Your Brand Colours

Incorporate your main and secondary brand colours into wall art. Abstract pieces or custom prints in these shades can subtly reinforce brand identity without being overt. This works particularly well in reception areas and client-facing spaces, where first impressions matter most. Even a single piece in your brand's primary colour, hung in a prominent position, can anchor the room and make the space feel intentionally designed.

Reflect Your Brand Values

Consider the tone of your brand — are you cutting-edge, traditional, eco-friendly, or creative? The style of art, from sleek metalwork to warm handmade pieces, should speak to this. A sustainability-focused business might choose botanical prints or natural material wall panels, whilst a technology company might favour clean geometric abstracts in monochrome. The art doesn't need to explain your brand; it simply needs to feel consistent with it.

Incorporate Logos or Mission Statements

Subtle wall decal logos or framed mission statements add a professional touch. Partner them with artwork that complements rather than competes, keeping the overall wall arrangement balanced and uncluttered. For inspiration that balances professionalism with personalised style, our interior trends page offers guidance on styles that align with a range of brand aesthetics.

What Are the Best Office Wall Decor Ideas for a Professional Look?

A professional look in an office isn't just about neat desks or polished floors — wall decor plays a huge role in shaping the space's atmosphere. For an office to look both sophisticated and inviting, you need the right office wall decor ideas. The most consistently professional spaces share three qualities: restraint in the number of pieces displayed, consistency in framing and finish, and art that feels considered rather than accidental.

Neutral Colour Schemes

Choosing neutral colours such as greys, whites, blacks, and navy for your wall art creates a timeless backdrop that looks refined. Subtle pops of colour can be added through accessories or smaller pieces. Neutral-toned art also has the practical advantage of working across different office layouts and furniture styles, making it a safe long-term investment that won't clash as the space evolves.

Abstract and Geometric Art

Abstract shapes or geometric prints offer a modern, professional look. They provide visual interest without being disruptive or distracting during focused work. Sets of two or three coordinated abstract prints in the same colour family are particularly effective above a desk or along a corridor wall, creating a sense of visual rhythm that feels intentional and polished.

High-Quality Materials

Invest in framed art with quality finishes, like glass glazing and solid wood frames. This improves longevity and maintains a smart appearance over time. Cheap frames with visible joins or warping can undermine even excellent artwork, so it's worth spending a little more on the framing than on the print itself if budget is limited.

Minimalism is Key

Less is often more. A few carefully curated pieces spaced well avoid clutter and keep the office feeling open and inspiring. A useful rule of thumb is to leave at least as much empty wall as you fill — negative space is not wasted space, it is what gives each piece room to breathe and be noticed.


SHOP HERE

What Wall Art Styles Work Best for Different Office Rooms?

Understanding which wall art styles suit different office environments ensures the decor supports function as well as style. The right match between art style and room purpose makes a workspace feel intentional rather than decorated by default. Here's a quick guide for matching styles with rooms.

Home Offices

Botanical and nature-themed pieces create calm and inspire mindfulness, making them ideal for spaces where you need to sustain focus over long periods. Minimal abstract art keeps attention sharp without distraction, and works particularly well in neutral-toned home offices where the art provides the only real visual accent. Choosing pieces with a consistent colour thread — even across different subjects — gives a home office gallery wall a pulled-together quality that feels professional without being corporate.

Conference Rooms

Bold geometric shapes emphasise structure and focus, which supports the kind of clear, decisive thinking that meetings require. Monochrome photography adds sophistication and timelessness, and tends to age well as office interiors evolve. Avoid art with strong narrative or emotional content in conference rooms — it can become a distraction or prompt unintended conversations during client meetings.

Creative Spaces

Mixed media and artistic collages fuel creative thinking and playfulness, making them the natural choice for studios, design rooms, and brainstorming spaces. Vibrant colours and patterns energise the environment and signal to the people working there that unconventional thinking is welcome. For versatile unique wall art that suits various styles and rooms, visit our dedicated office decor collection.

How Can I Decorate Office Walls on a Budget?

Stretching your budget to make your office walls look stylish and professional is achievable with a few clever ideas. Focus on maximising what you have and smart sourcing. The single most effective budget decision is to choose one genuinely good piece as your anchor and build around it with lower-cost items, rather than spending evenly across many mediocre pieces.

Printable Artwork and Framing

Start with downloadable prints — they're available in many styles and you can print them yourself or at local print shops. Pair prints with inexpensive yet stylish frames for a polished look. The key is consistency: choosing printables within the same colour family or visual style makes even a low-budget arrangement look curated and deliberate rather than assembled from whatever was available.

Use What You Have Creatively

Repurpose old frames by repainting or re-matting photographs and posters. Add washi tape designs or collage formats to personalise cheaply. Unifying a mixed collection of frames with a single coat of the same paint colour — all black, all white, or all natural wood — instantly gives the arrangement a gallery-like quality that looks far more expensive than it is.

Mix and Match Materials

Combine fabric wall hangings, cork boards for pinning ideas, and your printed artworks to inject personality without major expense. This layered approach also makes it easy to update the display over time without replacing everything at once. Affordable and stylish options are found through our office decor collection.

To Wrap Up

Transforming your office walls with thoughtful decor is one of the simplest ways to boost productivity, creativity, and overall well-being in your workspace. Whether you're working from home or managing a corporate office, the right wall art can make all the difference.

From trending styles and calming colour palettes to budget-friendly tips and brand-aligned choices, there are endless office wall decor ideas to suit every taste and need. Remember to choose pieces that inspire you, reflect your values, and create an environment where you can do your best work.

More About…

For further reading on how office environments affect productivity and well-being, Sharp's guide on office interior design and employee well-being is worth a read.

Key Rules for Office Wall Decor

  • Match art style to room function — calm for home offices, bold for conference rooms, eclectic for creative spaces
  • Use colour psychology — blues for focus, greens for creativity, neutrals for professionalism
  • One large statement piece often beats multiple small ones for impact and budget
  • Align art with brand colours and values for client-facing and reception spaces
  • Quality frames with glass glazing elevate even affordable prints significantly
  • Leave as much empty wall as you fill — negative space makes each piece more impactful

A breakfast nook is one of those simple ideas that can completely change how you feel about your home — turning a spare corner into a place you genuinely look forward to each morning. Whether you're working with a compact kitchen or a generous open-plan space, creating a dedicated dining nook is far more achievable than most people think. Have you ever dreamt of a cosy corner in your kitchen, bathed in morning light, perfect for that first cup of tea? That little sanctuary is a breakfast nook, and it’s so much more than just a table and chairs.

Quick Answer: A breakfast nook is a compact, dedicated dining area — typically tucked into a corner or bay window — designed for casual meals and morning routines. The key elements are space-saving seating (such as a banquette or bistro chairs), warm lighting, and personal décor like wall art or a mirror. Even a small kitchen can accommodate one with the right layout and furniture choices.

For me, it’s the heart of the home’s quiet moments. It’s where you can enjoy a peaceful breakfast, catch up on emails, or watch the kids do their homework.

This guide is here to give you friendly, actionable advice on how to make a breakfast nook that feels both personal and stylish.

How to Make a Breakfast Nook with Perfect Seating

The first practical step to make a breakfast nook is choosing the right seating. It sets the foundation for both comfort and style. In many UK homes where space can be a premium, built-in banquette seating for kitchen areas is a brilliant solution.

 It tucks neatly into a corner, maximising your floor space. Plus, many designs come with hidden storage underneath the seats, which is perfect for stashing away table linens, seasonal decor, or even board games. It instantly creates that cosy, restaurant-booth feeling.

However, if built-in isn't for you, there are other wonderful options.

A chic bistro set with two elegant chairs is perfect for a couple or a smaller household, offering flexibility and an airy, modern feel.

For those with a more open-plan living area, a plush, curved bench can create a sophisticated and conversational zone without needing a corner.

Using Wall Art to Make a Breakfast Nook Feel Special

What exactly is abstract art, and why has it become one of the most popular choices for home interiors? At its core, abstract art communicates emotion and atmosphere through colour, form, and texture rather than representing recognisable objects or scenes — which is precisely what makes it so adaptable to any room. From bold geometric prints to soft, fluid canvases, the range is extraordinary, and you don't need an art degree to find a piece that feels right for your space.

By Mae Osz | Interior Design Consultant & Home Decor Expert with 12+ years of experience.

Have you ever explored different Abstract Wall Art Ideas and noticed how they can turn even the plainest wall into a vibrant statement piece?

Quick Answer: Abstract art is a style that communicates ideas and emotions through colour, shape, line, and texture rather than depicting recognisable objects or scenes. It emerged as a major movement in the early 20th century and has remained a defining force in modern and contemporary art ever since. For home interiors, it is valued for its versatility — a single piece can set a room's entire mood without competing with furniture or décor.

Unlike traditional art that depicts familiar faces, objects, or places, abstract art relies on colour, shape, and movement to create mood and emotion.

What surprises many people is that abstract art doesn’t represent anything literal at all—it invites you to connect through feeling, letting every viewer discover their own meaning in the swirls, lines, and textures. And here’s the best part: you don’t need artistic expertise to understand or enjoy it.

Abstract art is made for personal interpretation, so anyone can find a connection that feels uniquely their own.

Quick Summary

Takeaway Explanation

Choose appropriate colour palettes for your space Colour impacts mood; select combinations that harmonise with your room’s existing scheme.

1: What Is Abstract Art and Why Does It Work in Any Space?

This style of art represents a fascinating realm of creative expression that transforms spaces through non-representational visual experiences. Unlike traditional art forms that depict recognisable objects or scenes, abstract art focuses on communicating emotions, concepts, and sensations through colour, shape, line, and texture.

According to the National Museum of Women in the Arts, abstract art emphasises the arrangement of visual elements to convey ideas and emotions rather than reproducing realistic imagery. This artistic approach allows for profound personal interpretation and emotional connection.

Key characteristics of abstract wall art include:

  • Emotional Resonance: Communicating feelings through non-literal visual language

  • Artistic Freedom: Liberating artists from representational constraints

  • Spatial Dynamism: Creating visual energy and movement within a static image

Understanding this style of art requires an open mindset and willingness to engage with artwork beyond literal representation. Each piece invites viewers to explore their personal emotional landscape, making non-representational wall art a powerful tool for transforming home décor. Whether minimalist and geometric or fluid and organic, these artworks can dramatically alter a room's atmosphere — for a deeper look at this effect, read our guide on how modern wall art reshapes contemporary home décor.

By embracing these kinds of pieces, you're not just decorating a space — you're curating an environment that speaks to your unique aesthetic sensibilities and emotional depth.

If you are drawn to bold, graphic compositions, you may also enjoy reading about how mid-century modern décor uses wall art as a conversational piece — a style that leans heavily on non-representational forms and strong colour contrasts.

2: Choose Your Colour Palette

Selecting the perfect colour palette for your wall art is an intricate process that transforms spaces and evokes powerful emotional responses. According to the National Design Academy, colour is a sophisticated design tool capable of setting an entire room’s mood before any furniture is introduced.

When exploring abstract wall art colour palettes, consider these strategic approaches:

  • Complementary Colours: Create dynamic visual tension by selecting opposite colours on the colour wheel

  • Monochromatic Schemes: Develop depth and sophistication using variations of a single colour

  • Neutral Foundations: Use subtle tones as a backdrop for more expressive artistic elements

Emotional Colour Psychology plays a significant role in palette selection. Warm tones like oranges and reds generate energy and passion, while cool blues and greens promote calmness and introspection. Each colour communicates a unique narrative within your chosen piece.

Consider your existing room's colour scheme when selecting wall art. Discover interior decor ideas that harmonise your artwork with surrounding elements, creating a cohesive visual experience.

Natural and artificial light can transform the artwork's appearance throughout the day, adding another layer of visual complexity to any piece you hang.

3: Consider Different Mediums and Textures

Abstract wall art transcends traditional two-dimensional representations by exploring diverse mediums and textures that create rich, multisensory experiences. According to research from Coventry University, artistic practices have evolved to embrace innovative materials and experimental techniques.

Exploring different mediums offers unique opportunities for artistic expression:

  • Canvas Paintings: Traditional yet versatile, allowing layered paint techniques

  • Mixed Media Compositions: Combining materials like fabric, metal, and found objects

  • Digital Prints: Precise, contemporary representations with crisp visual clarity

Texture plays a crucial role in abstract wall art, transforming flat surfaces into dynamic visual landscapes. Raised acrylic paints, textured canvases, and relief techniques can create depth that invites tactile exploration. Some artists incorporate unconventional materials like sand, metallic leaf, or handmade paper to add intricate dimensionality.

When selecting textural abstract art, consider how the piece interacts with your space. If you’re struggling with a room that feels monotonous, explore strategies for adding visual interest through carefully chosen wall art.

Remember that texture can dramatically alter an artwork’s emotional impact. Smooth, sleek surfaces communicate minimalist sophistication, while rough, uneven textures suggest raw emotional intensity. The medium you choose becomes a language that speaks beyond colour and form.


Shop Here

4: How to Evaluate and Choose the Right Piece for Your Home

Engaging with art communities provides invaluable insights and inspiration for discovering exceptional abstract wall art. According to Tate’s comprehensive art resources, connecting with local and digital art networks can transform your artistic understanding and collection approach.

Strategic ways to immerse yourself in art communities include:

  • Local Art Galleries: Attend exhibitions and meet artists directly

  • Online Art Platforms: Explore virtual galleries and artist portfolios

  • Social Media Art Groups: Connect with creators worldwide

Digital Platforms have revolutionised how we discover and interact with abstract art. Instagram, Pinterest, and specialised art websites offer unprecedented access to emerging artists and unique abstract wall art collections. These platforms allow you to explore diverse styles, understand artistic trends, and connect directly with creators.

Local art communities provide equally rich experiences. Regional galleries, art fairs, and community workshops offer opportunities to engage personally with abstract art creators. These interactions provide deeper context about artistic techniques, inspirations, and the stories behind individual pieces.

When exploring these communities, approach with curiosity and openness. Each interaction can provide unique perspectives on abstract wall art, helping you develop a more nuanced appreciation for this dynamic art form. Discover new interior decor inspirations that emerge from these creative connections and transform your living spaces.

    5: Mix and Match with Other Art Styles

    Mixing abstract wall art with diverse artistic styles creates dynamic, multi-dimensional visual narratives that transform living spaces. According to Cambridge psychological research, engaging with diverse art styles can enhance abstract thinking and broaden our perceptual understanding.

    Key strategies for successful art style integration include:

    • Complementary Contrasts: Pair abstract pieces with minimalist or traditional artworks

    • Colour Harmony: Select art with shared colour palettes

    • Balanced Composition: Create visual dialogue between different art styles

    Layering different artistic approaches allows you to craft unique visual experiences. For instance, combine a bold abstract canvas with delicate line drawings, or juxtapose geometric abstract art against soft, impressionistic watercolours. These unexpected combinations generate visual tension and intellectual intrigue.

    Consider your space’s existing aesthetic when mixing art styles.     6: Frame and Display Your Art Creatively

    Framing and displaying abstract wall art transforms mere artwork into a powerful design statement that breathes life into your living spaces. According to Hertfordshire Visual Arts, thoughtful art presentation can dramatically enhance the aesthetic impact of your chosen pieces.

    Key considerations for creative art display include:

    • Gallery Wall Arrangements: Create dynamic visual narratives

    • Unconventional Mounting: Explore floating frames and alternative hanging techniques

    • Strategic Lighting: Highlight artwork’s unique textures and colours

    Framing techniques offer endless possibilities for personalisation. Minimalist metallic frames can provide a contemporary edge to abstract pieces, while wooden frames with organic textures complement more textural artworks. Consider matching frame colours to room accents or selecting contrasting tones that create visual intrigue.

    For challenging spaces like staircases or awkward wall angles, explore innovative hanging solutions that transform architectural limitations into creative opportunities.

    Remember that art display is an evolving practice. Don’t be afraid to experiment, rotate pieces seasonally, and allow your living space to tell a dynamic, ever-changing visual story. The right presentation can elevate abstract wall art from mere decoration to a profound personal expression.

    7: Tailor Art Choices to Each Room’s Purpose

    Selecting abstract wall art requires thoughtful consideration of each room’s unique atmosphere and functional purpose. According to Art UK, artwork should harmonise with the room’s intended emotional and practical experience.

    Room-specific art selection strategies include:

The artwork becomes more than decoration – it’s an atmospheric conductor.

    9: A Brief History of Abstract Art

    Abstract art as a formal movement emerged in Europe during the early 20th century, driven by artists who wanted to move beyond representing the physical world. Wassily Kandinsky is widely credited as one of the first painters to create purely non-representational works, around 1910, arguing that colour and form could express spiritual and emotional truths on their own. Movements such as Cubism, Expressionism, and later Abstract Expressionism in mid-century America each pushed the boundaries of what art could mean without depicting anything literal.

Today, prints inspired by these movements are among the most searched and purchased wall art styles in the UK, prized for their ability to complement almost any interior without feeling dated.

Choosing curtains to go with grey walls is one of the most common — and most rewarding — decorating decisions you can make. Grey is endlessly versatile, but that neutrality means curtains do a lot of the heavy lifting: they set the warmth, contrast, and mood of the whole room. Whether you're working with a pale silver-grey bedroom or a dramatic charcoal living room, the right curtain colour can either tie everything together or unbalance it entirely. Here's what you need to know before you choose. 

Have you ever stood in a room painted in varying shades of grey and wondered what colour curtains for grey walls would best bring the space to life? Perhaps you've hesitated before choosing curtain hues, worried about clashing undertones or dull aesthetics. Grey walls can be a wonderfully versatile backdrop, but styling them with curtains requires a thoughtful approach to get that perfect balance of warmth, contrast, and harmony. Let's explore how to master what color curtains for grey walls like a professional designer—whether your walls are soft dove grey or a dramatic charcoal.

Quick Answer: The best curtains to go with grey walls depend on the shade and undertone of your grey. Warm neutrals like cream, taupe, and blush work beautifully with cool-toned greys, while jewel tones such as emerald green or navy add striking contrast. For dark or charcoal grey walls, lighter curtains in soft white or warm linen will brighten the space without clashing.

Grey walls offer an ideal canvas for art and accessories. Pairing curtains with this neutral tone shapes the entire mood of your room. Since you value mindful interiors and calming spaces, choosing the right curtain colours lets you enhance your living room decor or bedroom sanctuary with ease. The right curtains create a flow and softness that complements your wall art and furnishings. With a few expert insights on undertones, fabric, and colour combinations, you're closer than ever to designing an inviting and cohesive room.

List of Contents

  • How to Choose the Right Curtain Colour for Grey Walls
  • Understanding Undertones in Grey Walls and Curtains
  • Best Fabric Choices for Curtains Accompanying Grey Walls
  • Colour Combinations That Work — and a Few to Avoid
  • How to Use Curtains to Transform Light in Spaces with Grey Walls
  • White Curtains With Grey Walls: Fresh, Modern and Always Right

Curtain Colour Selection for Grey Walls: Professional Tips

Choosing what color curtains for grey walls boils down to understanding the impact of warmth, contrast, and cohesiveness. Grey's neutrality invites both subtle and striking curtain colours, but with the right approach, you can bring out the best in your space.

Neutral Curtain Colours: The Safe Haven

For those who love a calming and mindful room, warm neutrals and soft whites work beautifully against grey walls. Consider shades like ivory, cream, taupe, or even soft blush which add gentle contrast without overpowering.

  • Ivory or cream curtains bring warmth to cooler grey tones predominantly found in many modern interiors.
  • Soft taupe blends beautifully with mid-tone greys, enhancing a sophisticated palette without causing dullness.
  • Blush hues add a touch of subtle femininity while maintaining the room's calming energy.

Bold and Vibrant Accents

Looking to make a statement? Bold jewel tones like deep teal, emerald green, or even muted mustard can transform the atmosphere, especially in rooms with ample natural light. These colours introduce energy while maintaining style integrity.

Using Patterns for Added Depth

Incorporating curtains with gentle patterns such as geometric designs or soft floral prints can also enliven grey walls. Be mindful to keep patterns subtle so they won't clash with your wall art or interior design concepts.

Remember this key advice: When in doubt, start with your wall art and furniture tones, then select curtain hues that either complement or provide balanced contrast.


Shop Now

Understanding Undertones in Grey Walls and Curtains

If you are building out a full neutral scheme, our complete guide to styling a grey and beige living room pairs perfectly with these curtain choices. Pinpointing the undertone can simplify your selection process.

Common Undertones in Grey Walls

Grey Undertone Description Recommended Curtain Colours Colours to Avoid
Blue undertone Cool, crisp, often found in light or medium greys Warm creams, beige, blush; soft aubergine Cool greys, black, bright blue
Green undertone Muted and earthy, common in mid-tone greys Rich browns, olive, terracotta Bright white, pastel pinks
Warm beige undertone Look for a slightly warm or sandy cast Warm taupe, mustard, warm greys Cold blues, purples

Knowing the undertone means choosing curtains that either complement or add welcome warmth. For instance, if your walls have blue undertones, pairing them with creams or blush curtains warms the room. Conversely, matching cool undertones with similar cool curtains can sometimes feel cold.

Best Fabric Choices for Curtains Accompanying Grey Walls

Fabric dramatically affects curtain appearance and mood. When considering what color curtains for grey walls, the fabric's weight, texture, and light-filtering ability matter.

Light Fabrics for Airiness and Softness

  • Linen offers understated elegance with a soft texture that brings casual warmth, ideal for light or mid grey walls.
  • Cotton voile or sheer adds a layer of airiness, perfect for natural light spaces, softening the hard edges of grey.

Heavier Fabrics for Depth and Insulation

  • Velvet makes a plush statement, especially in deep or charcoal greys; ideal with rich jewel tones.
  • Thermal curtains add warmth and sound insulation, great for bedrooms, and typically come in muted warm tones.

Mixing Textures

For layered styling, pairing heavier curtains with sheers or blending different textures with your wall art can create visual interest.


Shop Now

Colour Combinations to Avoid with Grey Walls

Even though grey walls are flexible, some curtain colours can jar or clash. Steering clear of these combinations will save you from a disjointed look.

  • Too much cold on cold: Pairing cold blues or blacks with cool grey walls risks creating a gloomy, lifeless space.
  • Neon and overly bright colours: These punchy, synthetic hues can overwhelm grey's subtlety and clash with delicate wall art.
  • Matching too closely: Layering many similar shades of grey without variation in texture or tone may feel flat or boring.

Instead, draw on expert colour combinations concepts, and add contrast, texture, or warmth for best results.

For a complete grey decorating scheme, it also helps to think beyond curtains — our room-by-room guide to colors that go well with grey covers everything from warm neutrals and pastels to bold accent choices.

How to Use Curtains to Transform Light in Spaces with Grey Walls

Light shapes how we see colour, especially on grey walls. When learning what color curtains for grey walls work best, consider your space's natural light and how curtains affect it.

Bright Spaces With Abundant Light

In rooms flooded with sunlight, heavier or textured curtains in warm tones can add comfort without blocking brightness. Light fabrics like sheers let the light gently diffuse and soften the grey, making your room feel welcoming.

Low-Light or North-Facing Rooms

Dark grey walls in dimmer areas benefit from curtains that reflect light back in. Whites, creams, or soft warm colours help brighten the room. Stay away from dark or heavily patterned curtains that consume the limited light.

Control and Flexibility

  • Use layered curtains combining a sheer base with heavier drapes for best of both worlds.
  • Choose curtain track systems for smooth operation, matching the understated elegance of your styling tips.

What color curtains go best with light grey walls?

Light grey walls are wonderfully adaptable and set a serene tone for any room. When deciding what color curtains for grey walls in this shade, your best bet includes warm neutrals and soft pastels.

Cream, ivory, or light taupe curtains inject a welcoming warmth without disrupting the airy feel. Soft pinks or gentle peach tones also harmonise beautifully if you want a subtle splash of colour. These choices maintain the room's calming atmosphere and work well with natural wooden or pale furnishings.

If you prefer a bit more contrast, dusty blue or sage green curtains add a muted colour pop that brings personality without overwhelming the light grey backdrop. These cooler tones stay sophisticated but avoid the room feeling cold or sterile.

Styling example: One client chose linen beige curtains paired with a grey living room featuring white framed wall art and light oak furniture, perfectly encapsulating a bright Scandi aesthetic. This combination made their space feel warmer and more inviting without sacrificing the elegance of the pale grey walls.


Shop Now

What curtain colors make grey walls look warmer?

If your goal is to bring warmth into a grey-walled room, choosing curtains in colours with warmer undertones is key. Since cool greys can sometimes feel distant, warm curtains soften and enliven the space.

Rich terracotta, mustard yellow, rust, or burnt orange are excellent choices. These colours add vibrancy and create an inviting atmosphere. Even soft blush and warm caramel shades work well, especially in rooms emphasising natural materials and textures.

These warm curtains can also highlight the natural undertones in your walls if present—especially if the walls have subtle beige or greenish hints.

Case in point: A homeowner with grey walls chose deep rust-coloured velvets. This addition instantly transformed a light-filled living room into a cosy retreat while complementing existing framed wall art in natural tones. This layering reflects expert styling tips and design principles.

Do white curtains work with dark grey walls?

Absolutely! White curtains are a classic choice with dark grey walls. They create striking contrast that lifts the room's mood and introduces a fresh, clean aesthetic.

Choose crisp whites or even off-white tones to avoid harshness. Linen or cotton fabrics add texture that prevents the white from feeling too stark against dark grey. This combo balances drama with lightness perfectly, especially in contemporary or minimalist interiors.

White curtains also allow framed wall art to stand out clearly, creating a gallery-like atmosphere. By pairing dark walls with white curtains, you maintain a calming yet visually interesting space that honours your aesthetic preferences.

What color curtains match grey walls and grey furniture?

When the room features both grey walls and grey furniture, layering in curtain colour is essential for depth and warmth. Monochromatic schemes can work but often risk feeling cold or flat.

To avoid this, bring in curtains with a slight warmth or subtle colour variation like warm beige, soft camel, or muted blush tones. These add enough contrast to stand out yet keep the space unified.

Another option is textured curtains in rich materials such as velvet or linen blends. Texture adds dimensionality that plain colour alone cannot achieve. Jewel tones like emerald or sapphire can also work if you want a richer palette and contrast with the room's greys.

For example, a designer paired mid-tone grey walls and charcoal sofas with warm beige curtains and brass accessories. This combo created an inviting, layered look that's ideal for relaxing or entertaining.

For additional inspiration, explore our styling tips and curated living room decor collections to find beautiful coordinating accessories that complete your look.

Here is a quick reference table summarising curtain colour ideas for grey walls and furniture:

Room Elements Recommended Curtain Colours Comments
Light grey walls + neutral furniture Warm cream, soft blush, beige Softens grey, creates a gentle contrast
Dark grey walls + grey furniture White, warm beige, jewel tones Adds brightness and depth
Mid-tone grey walls + grey furniture Terracotta, mustard, textured neutrals Brings warmth, texture adds interest

These choices help you navigate what color curtains for grey walls and grey furniture create harmony and style.

WATCH The ULTIMATE Guide to Beautiful Wall Decor

To wrap up

Choosing what color curtains for grey walls isn't daunting when you understand the shades, undertones, fabrics, and lighting at play. From warm neutrals and dusty pastels that enhance light grey walls to rich warm tones that add cosiness, the options are generous and beautiful. Remember to consider your room's natural light and the colours already present in furniture and accessories. Curtains are more than functional—they're a key design element helping you craft calm, inviting, and personalised interiors.

So next time you're considering curtains, think beyond the basics; use colour, texture, and fabric to refresh your living space. Its your chance to add softness, warmth, or a splash of drama to complement your curated wall art and decor choices. With these tailored tips, you'll feel more confident mastering what color curtains for grey walls like a professional designer and transforming your home into a stylish sanctuary.

What do the most talked-about interior trends of 2026 actually look like in a real home — and which ones are already fading before they've had a chance to settle? This year's dominant shifts are rooted in warmth, sustainability, and a quiet pushback against cold, overly polished spaces. Think earthy palettes, natural textures, and designs that feel genuinely lived-in rather than showroom-perfect. Read on for a clear, practical guide to what's worth embracing and what's best left behind. 

By Mae Osz | Interior Design Consultant & Home Decor Expert with 12+ years of experience.

Quick Answer: The leading interior trends for 2026 centre on earthy colour palettes (terracotta, warm ochre, muted greens), natural and sustainable materials (rattan, reclaimed wood, linen), and styles that balance warmth with simplicity — particularly Japandi, warm maximalism, and wabi-sabi. Cold minimalism, high-gloss finishes, and overly stark monochrome schemes are on the way out. The overall direction is towards spaces that feel calm, personal, and authentically lived-in.

Have you ever stepped into a room and instantly felt calm, inspired, or simply at home? Interior design trends powerfully influence these emotions, and with 2026 here, it's the perfect time to refresh your space. Whether you're sprucing up a cosy reading nook or reimagining your entire living room, knowing what's in vogue — and what's fading — helps you create atmospheres you love for years.

As a fellow home decor enthusiast, I often find that great wall art ties a room's design together, making interiors truly personal. That's why keeping up with the interior design trends for 2026 isn't just about aesthetics — it's about crafting a mindful space where you can relax, express yourself, and feel connected to your surroundings.

From new colour palettes and textures to layout ideas that promote calm and balance, these trends influence everything from your furniture choices to the art you hang on your walls. So, let's take a friendly stroll through what's emerging in design to inspire your next home makeover.

List of Contents

  • The Biggest Style Shifts for 2026
  • Integrating Wall Art With 2026's Interior Design Trends
  • Key Takeaways:
  • 2025's Top Colours and How They're Evolving Into 2026

Top Interior Design Trends for 2026


Shop Here

The interior design trends for 2026 strike a refreshing balance between nature-inspired calm and modern refinement. Earthy colours like terracotta, soft clay, warm ochres, and muted greens are topping palettes. These shades connect indoor spaces to the outdoors, creating soothing environments.

Meanwhile, layered textures play a starring role — think woven baskets, stone surfaces, and velvety upholstery. These tactile elements add depth and invite mindfulness by encouraging touch and presence. If your home has mostly smooth finishes, try mixing in some natural textures through cushions or throws.

Material Shifts and Sustainable Touches

More than ever, eco-conscious choices shape design decisions. Rattan, bamboo, and reclaimed wood are popular materials, not only for their look but their sustainability. These materials often appear in furnishings, light fittings, and even wall decor.

Additionally, permaculture-inspired layouts promote calm and flow, guiding people through spaces intuitively. Open-plan areas remain favoured but with clever zoning using rugs, screens or plants to create functional, cosy corners.

Lighting as a Mood Creator

  • Soft, layered lighting combining pendants, floor lamps and candles
  • Warm white bulbs that mimic natural daylight
  • Statement light fixtures as subtle sculptures

Lighting is often the element that makes the biggest difference to how a room feels, yet it's the one most people address last. In 2026, the shift is towards treating lighting as a design decision in its own right — choosing a pendant that works as a sculptural object, or a floor lamp that creates a warm pool of light in a reading corner, rather than simply illuminating the room from above.

If you like, you can find further ideas in our collection of home decor trends on About Wall Art.

Natural Textures Rattan, wood grain, woven fabrics Furniture, baskets, cushions, wall hangings

Layered Lighting Multiple light sources at varying heights Living areas, bedrooms, dining rooms

What Styles Are In and Out for 2026?

Wondering which looks to embrace or leave behind? Here's an easy guide to freshen your home according to interior design trends for 2026.

In Style

  • Japandi: The fusion of Japanese minimalism with Scandinavian comfort continues to soar. Sleek, simple lines paired with warm, inviting textures promote balance.
  • Warm Maximalism: Unlike stark minimalism, this vibe layers rich colours and patterns — think warm ochres with floral or abstract prints. It's about personality and comfort, not clutter.
  • Wabi-Sabi: This Japanese aesthetic, embracing imperfection, encourages handcrafted objects, irregular shapes, and natural materials to foster a relaxed, honest space.
  • Art Deco Revival: Elegant geometric shapes and reflective metal accents add a subtle glamour that uplifts without overwhelming.

What these styles share is a commitment to warmth and authenticity — they all push back against the idea that a beautiful room needs to look untouched or perfectly curated. The best 2026 interiors feel like they belong to someone, with personality visible in every corner.

Out Style

  • Cold Minimalism: Strict, sterile white-on-white interiors are declining. People crave warmth and texture instead.
  • Overly Glossy Finishes: High-shine lacquer and plastic surfaces feel dated. Natural matte or soft finishes suit 2026 trends better.
  • Monochrome Extremes: Black and white only schemes lack the comforting touch that 2026 trends favour.
  • Fast Furniture: Cheap, disposable pieces are falling out as sustainable, durable options gain respect.

The common thread running through what's fading is a lack of warmth — these styles prioritised visual impact over how a room actually feels to live in. The 2026 shift is fundamentally about comfort and authenticity, which is why the styles moving out tend to be those that looked impressive in photographs but felt cold in person.

Of course, blending your personal favourites with these trends creates the best result for your home's spirit. For inspiration, visit our home decor trends page for ideas that resonate with you.

How Do You Future-Proof Your Interiors?

It's tempting to overhaul your home completely with every new wave of interior design trends. Yet, some adjustments are investments, not just decor fads. Here are my best tips to future-proof your interiors:

Invest in Quality Basics

Choose furniture made from durable, sustainable materials. Timeless silhouettes in neutral tones act as foundations you can accessorise. A well-made sofa in a warm linen or a solid wood dining table will outlast any trend cycle and look better with age — which is exactly the quality that 2026 interiors celebrate.

Layer With Trendy Accessories

Use rugs, cushions, and wall art to riff on the latest styles. Swapping these is far easier than replacing big-ticket items. A new set of cushions in terracotta and sage, or a fresh framed print above the sofa, can shift the entire mood of a room for a fraction of the cost of new furniture.

Adaptable Layouts

Flexible living spaces suited to multiple purposes (like home office or study nook) keep your home feeling relevant and welcoming. Black & white bathroom ideas have stood the test of time precisely because the combination works in almost any space — compact ensuite or generous family bathroom, Victorian terrace or modern new-build. The real challenge isn't choosing the palette; it's knowing how to balance contrast, texture, and scale so the result feels considered rather than cold. In this guide you'll find practical design advice covering tiles, fixtures, storage, lighting, and finishing touches to help you pull the look together with confidence.  

By Mae Osz | Interior Design Consultant & Home Decor Expert with 12+ years of experience.

Have you ever walked into a black and white bathroom and felt instantly captivated by its timeless elegance? There's something undeniably sophisticated about this classic colour combination that transforms ordinary bathrooms into stunning, spa-like retreats. Whether you're planning a complete renovation or a simple refresh, black and white bathroom ideas offer endless possibilities for creating a space that's both stylish and functional.

Quick Answer: Black and white bathrooms work in any size or style of home because the palette is inherently flexible — bold geometric tiles create drama, while soft white walls with black accents keep things calm and airy. The key is balancing contrast through texture, finish, and lighting rather than relying on colour alone. Layering matte and gloss surfaces, warm-toned bulbs, and carefully chosen accessories keeps the scheme feeling warm and inviting rather than stark.

In my experience helping homeowners design their perfect bathrooms, I've seen how the right balance of black and white elements—from tiles and fixtures to wall art and accessories—can completely elevate the space. The beauty lies in the versatility: you can go bold and dramatic or soft and minimalist, all whilst maintaining that crisp, clean aesthetic.

Let's explore expert design tips and inspiration to help you create the perfect black and white bathroom.

List of Contents

  • Tile choices that set the tone
  • Fixtures and finishes: creating contrast that works
  • Storage solutions that keep the scheme clean
  • Lighting: softening contrast and adding depth
  • Accessories and wall art: adding personality
  • Bringing your monochrome bathroom together
  • Balance and contrast: getting the ratio right
  • Introducing a splash of colour or a complementary shade

Tile choices that set the tone

Tiles set the foundation for your black and white bathroom. From classic subway tiles to bold geometric patterns, your choice dramatically impacts the overall feel.

For a ready-made solution, this set of three bathroom wall art black and white prints in French Country style is an easy way to bring that finishing touch to your walls.

Popular Tile Patterns

  • White subway tiles with black grout for definition
  • Checkerboard floors for vintage charm
  • Hexagon tiles for modern appeal
  • Herringbone patterns for visual interest

Shop Now

Fixtures and finishes: creating contrast that works

Black fixtures create striking contrast against white tiles and surfaces. Matte black taps, shower heads, and towel rails add modern sophistication.

Mixing Finishes

Don't be afraid to mix black fixtures with chrome or brass accents for added depth and interest.


Shop Now

Storage solutions that keep the scheme clean

Keep your black and white bathroom clutter-free with smart storage that complements the colour scheme.

Storage Ideas

  • Floating white shelves with black brackets
  • Black ladder shelves for towels
  • Built-in white niches with black trim
  • Wall-mounted black cabinets

Lighting: softening contrast and adding depth

Proper lighting is crucial in black and white bathrooms. Layer ambient, task, and accent lighting to create depth and prevent the space from feeling stark.

Lighting Tips

Use warm white bulbs to soften the contrast and create a welcoming atmosphere. Black pendant lights or sconces add style whilst providing functional lighting.


Shop Now

Accessories and wall art: adding personality

The finishing touches bring personality to your black and white bathroom. Wall art, plants, and carefully chosen accessories complete the look.

Wall art, plants, and carefully chosen accessories complete the look — for practical guidance on choosing prints that survive bathroom humidity, see our guide to beautiful bathroom art prints.

Accessorising Your Space

Black-framed mirrors, white towels with black trim, and moisture-resistant wall art add the perfect finishing touches. Plants in white or black pots bring life and warmth to the monochrome palette.

Bringing your monochrome bathroom together

Creating the perfect black and white bathroom is about finding the right balance between bold contrast and timeless elegance. By carefully selecting tiles, fixtures, storage, lighting, and finishing touches, you can design a bathroom that's both stunning and functional—a space you'll love for years to come.

Are black and white bathrooms still in style?

Absolutely — and for good reason. Unlike trend-led colour palettes that date quickly, a monochrome bathroom scheme is rooted in contrast and geometry, two design principles that transcend fashion cycles. Interior designers consistently return to black and white because it works as a neutral backdrop for any decorative style, from classic Victorian to pared-back Japandi.

What has evolved is how the combination is applied. Today's approach favours textural contrast — pairing matte tiles with gloss fixtures, rough stone with smooth porcelain — over the simple checkerboard patterns of earlier decades. This layering of finish and material is what keeps the look feeling current rather than dated.

Balance and contrast: getting the ratio right

One of the most common mistakes in a monochrome bathroom is applying black and white in equal measure. A more considered approach is to choose a dominant tone — usually white — and use the secondary colour as an accent. A ratio of roughly 70% white to 30% black creates a bright, airy feel; reversing those proportions delivers a more dramatic, cocoon-like atmosphere.

Contrast can also be introduced through texture rather than colour. A white wall covered in matt subway tiles reads very differently to the same wall clad in polished marble, even though both are technically white. Mixing surfaces — rough against smooth, matte against gloss — adds the visual depth that prevents a monochrome scheme from feeling flat.

Introducing a splash of colour or a complementary shade

A strictly black and white bathroom is a bold commitment. Many homeowners find that introducing a single complementary shade — warm brass, deep navy, or soft sage green — prevents the scheme from feeling clinical without compromising the monochrome foundation. The key is restraint: one accent colour, applied consistently through towels, plants, or a single feature tile, is far more effective than several competing tones.

Natural materials serve a similar softening function. Timber bath panels, rattan storage baskets, or a teak shower mat introduce warmth and organic texture that balances the sharpness of black and white without pulling the colour scheme off course.

Adding a carefully chosen monochrome art print is one of the simplest ways to introduce that final layer of visual interest without disrupting the palette.

What should you actually put above the toilet? No drilling is needed if you use adhesive strips, tension shelves, or leaning decor instead.

For a calming bathroom atmosphere, consider botanical prints, minimalist black and white photography, or abstract watercolour art. The goal is to choose pieces that complement your bathroom's colour palette whilst introducing a unique character. Artwork that references nature — leaves, botanicals, water — tends to feel particularly at home in a bathroom setting and never looks out of place as the rest of the room evolves.

Artwork above the toilet can become the highlight of your bathroom, especially when paired with coordinated bathroom decor options. Thoughtful selection enhances aesthetic expression without overcrowding the walls.

Balancing Storage and Style in Above Toilet Decor

Adding storage above the toilet is advantageous, especially in compact bathrooms. However, balancing storage with a stylish look is critical to avoid clutter and maintain the calming atmosphere you want. The key is to treat every item on display as a deliberate choice rather than a default — if it doesn't serve a purpose or add something visually, it probably doesn't need to be there.

Layered Storage Systems

Layer shelves with baskets and decorative items. This approach divides storage visually to maintain neatness whilst keeping frequently used items handy. For instance, place toiletries in baskets on the lower shelf and display attractive decor pieces like framed art on the top. The layered approach also makes it easy to refresh the look seasonally without changing the structure.

Choose Style-Friendly Storage Solutions

  • Opt for storage solutions like sleek floating shelves or built-in cubbies that match bathroom textures.
  • Use neutral tones to maintain harmony or glass shelving to keep the area light and open.

Keep Essentials Organised

Use containers or boxes for small items to avoid a messy surface. Remember, the goal is to add storage without making the space feel cramped. Decanting everyday items into matching containers — even simple white ceramic pots — instantly elevates the look and makes the shelf feel curated rather than utilitarian.

Combining storage and style this way complements your existing unique home decor, making everyday essentials accessible yet beautifully organised.

What are the best above toilet decor ideas for small bathrooms?

Small bathrooms pose decorating challenges, but the space above your toilet offers a prime opportunity to add both style and function without overcrowding. Here are my favourite above toilet decor ideas for small bathrooms:

Slim Floating Shelves

Choose narrow floating shelves that won't protrude too much. These provide room for essentials like scented candles, small potted plants, or a few decorative items without taking up space. Keeping the shelf depth under 20cm ensures it stays proportional to the toilet below and doesn't feel imposing.

Mirrors to Reflect Light

Adding a small, stylish mirror above the toilet can open up the space visually. Circular or uniquely shaped mirrors add charm and make your bathroom feel bigger. They also bounce natural light around the room, which is particularly valuable in bathrooms without windows.

Vertical Storage Units

If you want more storage, consider vertical wall-mounted shelving units. They're slim but maximise the vertical space efficiently. Going vertical rather than horizontal is the single most effective strategy for adding storage in a small bathroom without making it feel smaller.

Wall-Mounted Baskets

Utilise woven baskets attached to the wall for holding extra toilet rolls or small linens. They add texture without weight. A pair of matching baskets at different heights creates a simple, considered arrangement that feels intentional rather than improvised.

Minimal Clean Lines

Keep decoration minimal and consistent with your bathroom style. Avoid clutter by selecting fewer, meaningful pieces that complement the room's aesthetic. In a small bathroom, every item is visible from every angle — so each piece needs to earn its place.


Shop Here

How do you decorate above the toilet without drilling holes?


Shop Here

Many renters or those who prefer not to damage walls often ask, "How do you decorate above the toilet without drilling holes?" Fortunately, there are several practical options to beautify this space without permanent fixtures. The no-drill approach has improved enormously in recent years — modern adhesive products are strong enough to hold shelves, frames, and hooks securely in bathroom conditions.

Adhesive Shelves and Hooks

Modern adhesive shelves use strong, damage-free glue strips that can hold lightweight items such as plants, candles, or small storage containers. The key is selecting products designed for bathroom humidity and weight limits. Always check the maximum load rating before hanging anything heavier than a small plant or candle.

Tension Rod Shelving

A tension rod setup between walls above the toilet can support hanging baskets or lightweight shelves. This method requires no drilling and can be easily removed. It works particularly well in alcove bathrooms where the walls are close enough to create a stable tension fit.

Wall Decals and Temporary Art

To add personality without frames, use waterproof wall decals or removable sticky hooks for hanging lightweight prints or fabric art. Many removable decals are now designed specifically for humid environments and peel away cleanly without leaving residue.

Lean and Layer

Place leaning art or decorative trays on the toilet tank or slim cabinets nearby. This doesn't use the wall space but keeps the above area visually tidy. A small framed print leaning against the wall on a tank-top tray can look just as considered as a hung piece, with none of the commitment.

These no-drill methods allow you to personalise your space whilst respecting rental agreements and avoiding hassle.

What size artwork looks best for above toilet decor?


Shop Here

Picking the right artwork size is essential to create a well-balanced feature above your toilet. Generally, a piece that's too large overwhelms the space, whilst something too small will get lost. The goal is a piece that feels purposeful — clearly chosen for that spot rather than placed there by default.

Ideal Dimensions

Medium artworks around 40cm by 60cm are typically ideal. They align visually with the width of the toilet and fill the vertical space nicely without dominating the entire wall. If your ceiling is particularly high, a slightly taller piece or a stacked pair of prints can help fill the space without going too wide.

Gallery Walls or Groupings

If a single art piece feels too bold, combine several smaller framed prints (around 30cm square) grouped together. This arrangement adds interest without overpowering your bathroom. Treat the group as a single shape when planning the layout — the overall arrangement should sit within the same proportional guidelines as a single medium piece.

Spacing and Placement Tips

  • Leave a 15–20cm gap between the toilet tank and bottom of the artwork.
  • Keep the artwork centred horizontally above the toilet.
  • Consider vertical orientation if the wall is narrow.

Choosing the right size, like those found in our curated bathroom decor options, makes your above toilet decor feel intentional and harmonious.

How can above toilet decor add storage without cluttering the bathroom?

Add storage to your bathroom wisely, avoiding a cluttered look above the toilet. Achieving this balance requires strategic placement and selection of storage items. The most effective approach is to decide upfront how many items will live on each shelf and stick to it — creep is the enemy of a calm bathroom.

Use Baskets and Containers

Keep essentials organised inside baskets or storage boxes. These hide clutter yet create a tidy appearance, especially when colour-coordinated or matching bathroom textures. Matching containers — even simple ones — immediately make a shelf look more intentional and less like a dumping ground.

Limit the Number of Items

Display only frequently used or decorative items above the toilet. Store less-used toiletries elsewhere to keep the space from feeling overcrowded. A good rule is no more than five items per shelf — fewer if the shelf is narrow.

Opt for Open and Closed Storage

  • Use shelves combined with covered baskets or boxes.
  • Closed storage hides clutter but open shelves add visual interest.

Incorporate Style-Focused Storage

Choose storage that feels like decor — for example, woven baskets or stylish ceramic containers — which add personality and softness to the bathroom setting. When storage looks beautiful in its own right, the line between function and decoration disappears entirely, which is exactly the effect you're aiming for.

Key Takeaways:

  • The wall above your toilet is prime real estate — floating shelves, artwork, and baskets can transform it from blank to beautiful.
  • Medium artworks (40x60cm) are the ideal size for bathroom above toilet decor in most spaces.
  • Balance storage and style by layering baskets with decorative items — function doesn't have to mean clutter.
  • No-drill options like adhesive shelves and removable hooks make this accessible for renters too.
  • Keep small bathrooms feeling open by choosing slim shelves, minimal pieces, and light-reflecting mirrors.

Choosing the right size of a frame for wall art is one of those decisions that looks simple but catches a surprising number of people out. Go too small and the artwork looks lost; go too large and the frame dominates the wall. The good news is that with a few straightforward rules and some careful measuring, you can get it right first time — no guesswork needed.

Most people underestimate just how tricky it can be to get the size of a frame right for their wall art. I’ve found that guessing too small or too large can throw off the entire look of a room. The wrong size can indeed make your beautiful piece feel out of place.

Quick Answer: The ideal frame size depends on the dimensions of your artwork, the wall space available, and any matting you plan to include. As a general rule, the framed piece should cover 57–75% of the wall width it hangs on, and the frame border should be proportionate — wider borders suit smaller prints, narrower borders suit larger pieces. Always measure your wall and your artwork before buying a frame.

In this post, I’ll share the common pitfalls I’ve seen and how you can avoid them. Let's  ensure your wall art fits perfectly and enhances your space exactly as you imagine.

List of Contents

  • Understanding Frame Sizes and Proportions
  • How to Measure Your Wall Space Before Buying a Frame
  • Key Factors That Affect Your Frame Size Choice
  • Standard Frame Sizes at a Glance
  • Gallery Walls: Mixing and Matching Frame Sizes

Key Takeaways

  • The frame size should complement the wall art, not overpower or underwhelm it. Matching proportions helps create a balanced display.
  • Measuring the wall space carefully before choosing the frame prevents getting something too large or too small for the area.
  • Avoid guessing the frame size based on the artwork alone. Consider extra dimensions added by matting or the style of the frame.
  • Taking into account the room's overall décor and furniture scale helps the frame fit correctly — and pairing good frame proportions with the right wall colour makes an even bigger difference, so it is worth reading up on colour psychology principles for choosing wall colours.
  • Using templates or mock-ups can give a better idea of how different frame sizes will look once hung. 

Understanding Frame Sizes and Proportions

To get the perfect look for your wall art, understanding the dimensions of a frame is key. It’s not just about picking a frame that fits the artwork. It’s about finding one that enhances the piece and complements your space.

Frames that are too small can make artwork look cramped, while oversized frames might overpower the image or your room’s décor. I've found that paying attention to the balance between the frame, the art, and the wall space is central to how art shapes a room's mood and atmosphere — get the proportions right and the whole space feels more considered.

Choosing the right frame size also means considering the space where it will hang. I usually take measurements of the wall area and visualise how different sizes will fit within that space. This helps avoid surprises when the frame arrives and is ready to display. The perfect frame size supports your home's overall feel, making it look calm, elegant, and thoughtfully decorated, exactly what we all want when adding wall art.

How to Choose the Right Frame Size

If you’re wondering how to select the right size of a frame, start by measuring the artwork itself carefully. I recommend giving yourself a bit of extra room for any matting or spacing you plan to include. This helps the frame emphasise the art without crowding it. For instance, a small print usually does well with a slightly wider frame to give it presence, while a large piece might benefit from a slimmer frame to keep the focus on the art. 

Next, think about your wall space and how the framed piece fits in with other elements in the room. It’s helpful to lay out paper templates on the wall to see how different frame sizes look in your actual space. This simple trick saved me from buying frames that were either too imposing or too tiny for my walls. Finding the right size is all about achieving harmony between the artwork, frame, and room.

If you want to sidestep the sizing headache entirely, a 3 piece picture frame set is a straightforward solution — the prints are sized to work together, so you just need to measure your wall once and hang them as a trio.

Common Size Mistakes to Avoid

You might think that bigger is always better when it comes to frames, but that’s not true. One of the most frequent mistakes I’ve seen is choosing a frame that’s too large for the artwork, which can distract from the piece itself. On the other hand, frames that are too small can make your art look lost or insignificant. Another common error is not accounting for any matting or borders, which can throw off your measurements and leave you with ill-fitting frames.

Another pitfall is ignoring the wall space or grouping nearby artworks poorly. I’ve made this mistake before, hanging a large frame in a tight corner, which made the whole area feel crowded. It’s important to think about how the frame size interacts with the rest of your room’s layout to avoid disrupting the flow.

With careful planning, you can avoid these common errors that might leave your wall art looking less than ideal. Taking time to measure properly, thinking about the overall balance in the room, and considering any extras like mats can make a huge difference. Fixing these small but impactful details ensures your framed art looks its very best, bringing that creative, calming vibe you want in your home.

How to Measure Your Wall Space Before Buying a Frame

To find the perfect frame size, start by measuring your wall space. It sounds simple, but I’ve noticed that many people underestimate this step, leading to frames that feel too small or overpowering once hung. To avoid this, I always recommend using a tape measure to get accurate dimensions of the area where your wall art will hang. It’s helpful to take note of both width and height, and if you’re planning to hang multiple pieces, consider the total space they will occupy together.

Here are some handy tips to keep in mind when measuring your wall space:

  • Measure the wall at eye level where the artwork will be displayed.
  • Include space for the frame edges and any matting inside the frame.
  • Take measurements more than once to check accuracy.
  • Mark the wall with painter’s tape to visualise the artwork’s dimensions.
  • Keep your furniture and other room elements in mind to avoid clashes.

This approach helps me get a clear idea of the size that will look balanced and enhance my space.

How to Properly Measure Your Artwork

Artwork is the heart of your wall display, so measuring it properly is necessary. I always start by measuring the canvas or print itself, making sure to note the exact height and width without assuming the frame adds any extra dimension. Using a steel tape measure helps me get precise numbers, which is particularly important for larger or oddly shaped pieces.

Next, I add in the dimensions of the frame or matting you plan to use. Some frames can add several centimetres to the total size, so failing to include these extra elements can create surprises when you hang your art. Taking these steps ensures your chosen size of a frame complements the artwork perfectly and fits the intended space.

Considering the Space Around the Art

Measure the space around your art carefully to avoid crowding your walls. I find it helpful to leave a comfortable amount of blank space around the frame, so the art doesn’t feel squeezed or lost among other decorations. This ‘breathing room’ makes a big difference in how inviting and relaxing the space feels.

It's also worth thinking about the wall colour, lighting, and nearby furniture to make sure your chosen frame size works harmoniously within the room. When you consider these details, you create a balanced and inviting atmosphere that draws attention to your wall art and enhances your entire decor.

Understanding the space surrounding your wall art is just as important as the size of the frame itself. Leaving enough room around your artwork not only improves its impact but also helps maintain a calm and inspiring environment—something many of us value when decorating our homes.

Key Factors That Affect Your Frame Size Choice

Many elements come into play when deciding the size of a frame

When choosing the frame, it's helpful to think about:

  • The dimensions of your artwork itself
  • The size and style of the wall where it will hang
  • The overall décor and atmosphere you want to create
  • Lighting and how shadows might affect perception
  • Your personal style and how bold or subtle you’d like the frame to appear

Perceiving these factors enables you to make a confident choice that enhances both the artwork and your living space.

Artwork Types and Their Best Frame Sizes

An easy way to narrow down the size is by matching it to the type of artwork you’re displaying. Different kinds of wall art—like photography, paintings, prints, or textiles—often benefit from specific framing approaches that help them stand out or blend gently with their surroundings.

Here are some typical examples I often find helpful when selecting frame sizes based on artwork types:

  • Photography: Generally pairs well with sleek, minimal frames that don't distract

SHOP HERE

  • Paintings: Often require larger, more detailed frames to complement brush strokes and texture

  • Prints: Look best in medium-sized frames that balance the art without overwhelming it

SHOP HERE

  • Textile art: Benefit from deeper frames or shadow boxes to protect and highlight the fabric

After exploring these options, you’ll find it easier to decide on a frame size that suits your artwork perfectly.

Artwork Type

Recommended Frame Size

Photography

Simple, thin frame with minimal border

Paintings

Thicker, more ornate frames with a wider border

Prints

Moderate frame width to maintain balance

Textile Art

Shadow box or deep frame with protective glazing

Mixed Media

Custom frames matching the texture and size

 

The Role of Room Aesthetics in Frame Selection

Little details in your room’s design can have a surprising effect on how the frame feels once the artwork is hung. I have often seen how a frame that looks perfect in isolation suddenly feels out of place when matched with its surroundings. Factors like wall colour, furniture style, and even the room’s lighting all influence the right frame choice.

Choosing the right frame size also involves thinking about the scale of your room. Smaller rooms usually benefit from smaller, lighter frames to keep the space feeling open, while bigger spaces can handle bolder, larger frames that create a statement.

Plus, matching the size of a frame with your existing décor styles—whether that’s modern, rustic, or classic—can make a big difference in how cohesive your space feels. I've found that considering room aesthetics alongside artwork type brings harmony and lets your wall art truly shine without clashing or getting lost.

Standard Frame Sizes at a Glance

Knowing the most common frame dimensions before you shop saves a great deal of back-and-forth. Standard UK frame sizes are typically based on paper and print sizes, so your artwork will slot straight in without the need for custom cutting.

The most widely available sizes include A4 (21 × 29.7 cm), A3 (29.7 × 42 cm), A2 (42 × 59.4 cm), and A1 (59.4 × 84.1 cm). Imperial sizes such as 10×8 inch, 12×10 inch, and 20×16 inch are equally common, particularly for photographic prints. Choosing one of these standard dimensions keeps costs down and gives you far more frame styles to pick from.

If your print falls outside these measurements — for instance, a square format or a panoramic crop — you will either need a custom frame or a mat cut to bridge the gap. A well-cut mat can make a non-standard print fit neatly inside a standard frame, while also adding a polished, gallery-style finish. Browse our wall art prints to find designs sized to fit standard frames straight away.

Gallery Walls: Mixing and Matching Frame Sizes

A gallery wall lets you combine several prints in different sizes to create a cohesive display — but only if the proportions are planned carefully. Randomly hanging frames of varying sizes without a clear layout often results in a cluttered, unbalanced look that draws the eye in too many directions at once.

The most reliable approach is to anchor your gallery wall with one larger central piece, then build outward using medium and smaller frames. Keep the spacing between frames consistent — 5 to 8 cm between each is a good starting point — and aim for a unified colour or tone across the frames themselves. Mixing black, white, and natural wood frames can work beautifully, but limit yourself to two or three finishes at most.

Before you start hammering nails, lay the frames out on the floor to test your arrangement. Trace each frame onto paper, cut the templates out, and use masking tape to map the layout on your wall. This single step prevents a wall full of unwanted holes and gives you the freedom to adjust until the composition feels right. If you are looking for prints that are designed to work together, a set of 3 wall art prints takes the guesswork out of matching sizes.

Summing up

Hence, getting the size right is something I believe many of us can struggle with when choosing wall art. It’s easy to misjudge how big or small a frame will look in a room, but by thinking about the space, the furniture around it, and the art itself, you can avoid those common mistakes. Trust me, taking the time to visualise and measure properly makes all the difference in creating a harmonious and balanced look on your walls.

More About...

If you want to get a better feel for how to size your frames perfectly, I found this really helpful guide on How To Size Art For A Wall - Cattie Coyle Photography | Blog. It offers some practical tips and clear examples to help you make confident choices when picking the right frame size for your wall art. With the right approach, your framed pieces will enhance your space beautifully and feel just right.
